```plato
//==
// # Solids CSG
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Union, intersection, and difference of polygon soups
//  - Polygon-versus-plane classification and splitting
//  - Point-in-solid parity and fragmenting against a solid
//  - Deformation body for the polygon-soup solid

library SolidsCsg
{
    //==
    // # Union, intersection, and difference of polygon soups
    //
    // Boolean operations on closed `PolygonSoup3D` solids, the plane-clip
    // re-expression of csg.js: every boolean output is assembled from fragments of
    // A's faces cut by B's planes (so no fragment straddles B's boundary — see the
    // clipping section) and kept by whether the fragment's
    // centroid lies inside or outside B, plus the symmetric fragments of B against
    // A. Correct-over-fast: a boolean costs O(|A|^2 |B| + |B|^2 |A|); a BSP-tree
    // variant is a later, separate pass.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constructive_solid_geometry)
    //
    // Precondition throughout: both solids are closed, with convex CCW-outward
    // faces. Exactly coplanar shared faces of the two solids are the known
    // unreliable case (their fragment centroids sit ON the other boundary).

    // The fragments of a's faces, cut by b's planes, whose centroid's
    // insideness of b equals `keepInside`. The centroid of a convex fragment is
    // interior to it, so it classifies the whole fragment.
    KeptFragments(a: PolygonSoup3D, b: PolygonSoup3D, keepInside: Boolean): Array<Polygon3D>
        => a.Fragments(b.Planes, Number.CsgPlaneTolerance)
            .FlatMap(f => KeepPolygon(b.Contains(f.Centroid).ExclusiveOr(keepInside).Not, f));
```
